input: Apply for a food handler's certification online

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Food handler certification requirements vary significantly by country, state, or municipality — the correct issuing body and accepted program depend entirely on location.
There are different certification levels (basic food handler vs. food manager/supervisor); knowing which is required determines the course content and exam rigor.
Whether this is for the user personally or for multiple employees changes the account type, bulk pricing, and enrollment process.
Some employers or regulators require the certification by a specific date, which affects which providers are viable based on processing and delivery time.
The user may already have a provider in mind or be approved by a specific accredited platform; knowing this avoids redundant research into alternatives.
Some users want the cheapest option, others need a specific language, and others prioritize a fast self-paced exam — this shapes which platform to recommend.
Knowing whether the user needs a physical card, a digital certificate, or just proof of completion determines what counts as 'done' and which providers meet that standard.

gold.taskTitle: Apply for food handler's certification online
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to complete the process of obtaining a food handler's certification through an online platform.

questions.title: What country and state or province are you in?
questions.description: Food handler certification rules, accepted providers, and issuing bodies differ by jurisdiction. The user's location determines which programs are legally valid for them.

questions.title: Is this a basic food handler or food manager certification?
questions.description: Basic food handler cards and food protection manager certifications (e.g., ServSafe Manager) are different in scope, cost, and exam requirements. Clarifying the level keeps the plan focused.

questions.title: Is this certification for yourself or for multiple people?
questions.description: Individual enrollment vs. group/employee enrollment involves different account setups, potential bulk pricing, and administrative steps.

questions.title: Do you have a deadline by which you need the certification?
questions.description: Deadlines affect which providers are viable based on course length, exam scheduling, and certificate delivery or processing time.

questions.title: Has your employer or regulator specified an approved provider?
questions.description: Many employers and health departments only accept certificates from specific accredited platforms. Knowing this upfront avoids completing a course that will not be recognized.

questions.title: What matters most — lowest cost, fastest completion, or specific language?
questions.description: User priorities (price, speed, language availability) directly determine which of the several competing online platforms is the best fit.

questions.title: Do you need a physical card, a digital certificate, or either?
questions.description: Some workplaces or inspectors require a printed card; others accept a digital PDF or QR code. This determines what counts as successfully 'done' and narrows provider options accordingly.
